lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: CHAPTER VIII. The Queen’s Croquet-Ground

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A large rose-tree stood near the entrance of the garden: the roses growing on it were white, but there were three gardeners at it, busily painting them red. Alice thought this a very curious thing, and she went nearer to watch them, and just as she came up to them she heard one of them say,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “Look out now, Five! Don’t go splashing paint over me like that!”

lines.speaker: Five
lines.text: “I couldn’t help it,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Five, in a sulky tone;

lines.speaker: Five
lines.text: “Seven jogged my elbow.”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: On which Seven looked up and said,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “That’s right, Five! Always lay the blame on others!”

lines.speaker: Five
lines.text: “You’d better not talk!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Five.

lines.speaker: Five
lines.text: “I heard the Queen say only yesterday you deserved to be beheaded!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “What for?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the one who had spoken first.

lines.speaker: Seven
lines.text: “That’s none of your business, Two!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Seven.

lines.speaker: Five
lines.text: “Yes, it is his business!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Five,

lines.speaker: Five
lines.text: “and I’ll tell him—it was for bringing the cook tulip-roots instead of onions.”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Seven flung down his brush, and had just begun “Well, of all the unjust things—” when his eye chanced to fall upon Alice, as she stood watching them, and he checked himself suddenly: the others looked round also, and all of them bowed low.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Would you tell me,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice, a little timidly,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “why you are painting those roses?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Five and Seven said nothing, but looked at Two. Two began in a low voice,

lines.speaker: Five
lines.text: “Why the fact is, you see, Miss, this here ought to have been a red rose-tree, and we put a white one in by mistake; and if the Queen was to find it out, we should all have our heads cut off, you know. So you see, Miss, we’re doing our best, afore she comes, to—”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At this moment Five, who had been anxiously looking across the garden, called out “The Queen! The Queen!” and the three gardeners instantly threw themselves flat upon their faces. There was a sound of many footsteps, and Alice looked round, eager to see the Queen.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: First came ten soldiers carrying clubs; these were all shaped like the three gardeners, oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners: next the ten courtiers; these were ornamented all over with diamonds, and walked two and two, as the soldiers did. After these came the royal children; there were ten of them, and the little dears came jumping merrily along hand in hand, in couples: they were all ornamented with hearts. Next came the guests, mostly Kings and Queens, and among them Alice recognised the White Rabbit: it was talking in a hurried nervous manner, smiling at everything that was said, and went by without noticing her. Then followed the Knave of Hearts, carrying the King’s crown on a crimson velvet cushion; and, last of all this grand procession, came THE KING AND QUEEN OF HEARTS.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Alice was rather doubtful whether she ought not to lie down on her face like the three gardeners, but she could not remember ever having heard of such a rule at processions;

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “and besides, what would be the use of a procession,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: thought she,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “if people had all to lie down upon their faces, so that they couldn’t see it?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: So she stood still where she was, and waited.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: When the procession came opposite to Alice, they all stopped and looked at her, and the Queen said severely

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “Who is this?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She said it to the Knave of Hearts, who only bowed and smiled in reply.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “Idiot!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Queen, tossing her head impatiently; and, turning to Alice, she went on,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “What’s your name, child?”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “My name is Alice, so please your Majesty,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice very politely; but she added, to herself,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Why, they’re only a pack of cards, after all. I needn’t be afraid of them!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “And who are these?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Queen, pointing to the three gardeners who were lying round the rose-tree; for, you see, as they were lying on their faces, and the pattern on their backs was the same as the rest of the pack, she could not tell whether they were gardeners, or soldiers, or courtiers, or three of her own children.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “How should I know?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice, surprised at her own courage.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “It’s no business of mine.”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Queen turned crimson with fury, and, after glaring at her for a moment like a wild beast, screamed

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “Off with her head! Off—”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Nonsense!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice, very loudly and decidedly, and the Queen was silent.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The King laid his hand upon her arm, and timidly said

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “Consider, my dear: she is only a child!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Queen turned angrily away from him, and said to the Knave

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “Turn them over!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Knave did so, very carefully, with one foot.

lines.speaker: The Soldiers
lines.text: “Get up!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Queen, in a shrill, loud voice, and the three gardeners instantly jumped up, and began bowing to the King, the Queen, the royal children, and everybody else.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Leave off that!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: screamed the Queen.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “You make me giddy.”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: And then, turning to the rose-tree, she went on,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “What have you been doing here?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “May it please your Majesty,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Two, in a very humble tone, going down on one knee as he spoke,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “we were trying—”

lines.speaker: The Soldiers
lines.text: “I see!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Queen, who had meanwhile been examining the roses.

lines.speaker: The Soldiers
lines.text: “Off with their heads!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: and the procession moved on, three of the soldiers remaining behind to execute the unfortunate gardeners, who ran to Alice for protection.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “You shan’t be beheaded!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice, and she put them into a large flower-pot that stood near. The three soldiers wandered about for a minute or two, looking for them, and then quietly marched off after the others.

lines.speaker: The Soldiers
lines.text: “Are their heads off?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: shouted the Queen.

lines.speaker: The Soldiers
lines.text: “Their heads are gone, if it please your Majesty!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: the soldiers shouted in reply.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “That’s right!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: shouted the Queen.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Can you play croquet?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The soldiers were silent, and looked at Alice, as the question was evidently meant for her.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Yes!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: shouted Alice.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Come on, then!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: roared the Queen, and Alice joined the procession, wondering very much what would happen next.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “It’s—it’s a very fine day!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said a timid voice at her side. She was walking by the White Rabbit, who was peeping anxiously into her face.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Very,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice:

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “—where’s the Duchess?”

lines.speaker: Rabbit
lines.text: “Hush! Hush!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Rabbit in a low, hurried tone. He looked anxiously over his shoulder as he spoke, and then raised himself upon tiptoe, put his mouth close to her ear, and whispered

lines.speaker: Rabbit
lines.text: “She’s under sentence of execution.”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “What for?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice.

lines.speaker: Rabbit
lines.text: “Did you say ‘What a pity!’?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: the Rabbit asked.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “No, I didn’t,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice:

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I don’t think it’s at all a pity. I said ‘What for?’”

lines.speaker: Rabbit
lines.text: “She boxed the Queen’s ears—”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: the Rabbit began. Alice gave a little scream of laughter.

lines.speaker: Rabbit
lines.text: “Oh, hush!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: the Rabbit whispered in a frightened tone.

lines.speaker: Rabbit
lines.text: “The Queen will hear you! You see, she came rather late, and the Queen said—”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Get to your places!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: shouted the Queen in a voice of thunder, and people began running about in all directions, tumbling up against each other; however, they got settled down in a minute or two, and the game began. Alice thought she had never seen such a curious croquet-ground in her life; it was all ridges and furrows; the balls were live hedgehogs, the mallets live flamingoes, and the soldiers had to double themselves up and to stand on their hands and feet, to make the arches.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The chief difficulty Alice found at first was in managing her flamingo: she succeeded in getting its body tucked away, comfortably enough, under her arm, with its legs hanging down, but generally, just as she had got its neck nicely straightened out, and was going to give the hedgehog a blow with its head, it would twist itself round and look up in her face, with such a puzzled expression that she could not help bursting out laughing: and when she had got its head down, and was going to begin again, it was very provoking to find that the hedgehog had unrolled itself, and was in the act of crawling away: besides all this, there was generally a ridge or furrow in the way wherever she wanted to send the hedgehog to, and, as the doubled-up soldiers were always getting up and walking off to other parts of the ground, Alice soon came to the conclusion that it was a very difficult game indeed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The players all played at once without waiting for turns, quarrelling all the while, and fighting for the hedgehogs; and in a very short time the Queen was in a furious passion, and went stamping about, and shouting “Off with his head!” or “Off with her head!” about once in a minute.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Alice began to feel very uneasy: to be sure, she had not as yet had any dispute with the Queen, but she knew that it might happen any minute,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “and then,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: thought she,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “what would become of me? They’re dreadfully fond of beheading people here; the great wonder is, that there’s any one left alive!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She was looking about for some way of escape, and wondering whether she could get away without being seen, when she noticed a curious appearance in the air: it puzzled her very much at first, but, after watching it a minute or two, she made it out to be a grin, and she said to herself

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “It’s the Cheshire Cat: now I shall have somebody to talk to.”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “How are you getting on?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Cat, as soon as there was mouth enough for it to speak with.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Alice waited till the eyes appeared, and then nodded.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “It’s no use speaking to it,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she thought,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “till its ears have come, or at least one of them.”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: In another minute the whole head appeared, and then Alice put down her flamingo, and began an account of the game, feeling very glad she had someone to listen to her. The Cat seemed to think that there was enough of it now in sight, and no more of it appeared.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I don’t think they play at all fairly,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Alice began, in rather a complaining tone,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “and they all quarrel so dreadfully one can’t hear oneself speak—and they don’t seem to have any rules in particular; at least, if there are, nobody attends to them—and you’ve no idea how confusing it is all the things being alive; for instance, there’s the arch I’ve got to go through next walking about at the other end of the ground—and I should have croqueted the Queen’s hedgehog just now, only it ran away when it saw mine coming!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “How do you like the Queen?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Cat in a low voice.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Not at all,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice:

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “she’s so extremely—”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Just then she noticed that the Queen was close behind her, listening: so she went on,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “—likely to win, that it’s hardly worth while finishing the game.”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Queen smiled and passed on.

lines.speaker: Cat
lines.text: “Who are you talking to?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the King, going up to Alice, and looking at the Cat’s head with great curiosity.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “It’s a friend of mine—a Cheshire Cat,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice:

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “allow me to introduce it.”

lines.speaker: Cat
lines.text: “I don’t like the look of it at all,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the King:

lines.speaker: Cat
lines.text: “however, it may kiss my hand if it likes.”

lines.speaker: Cat
lines.text: “I’d rather not,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: the Cat remarked.

lines.speaker: Cat
lines.text: “Don’t be impertinent,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the King,

lines.speaker: Cat
lines.text: “and don’t look at me like that!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He got behind Alice as he spoke.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “A cat may look at a king,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I’ve read that in some book, but I don’t remember where.”

lines.speaker: Cat
lines.text: “Well, it must be removed,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the King very decidedly, and he called the Queen, who was passing at the moment,

lines.speaker: Cat
lines.text: “My dear! I wish you would have this cat removed!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Queen had only one way of settling all difficulties, great or small.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Off with his head!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she said, without even looking round.

lines.speaker: Cat
lines.text: “I’ll fetch the executioner myself,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the King eagerly, and he hurried off.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Alice thought she might as well go back, and see how the game was going on, as she heard the Queen’s voice in the distance, screaming with passion. She had already heard her sentence three of the players to be executed for having missed their turns, and she did not like the look of things at all, as the game was in such confusion that she never knew whether it was her turn or not. So she went in search of her hedgehog.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The hedgehog was engaged in a fight with another hedgehog, which seemed to Alice an excellent opportunity for croqueting one of them with the other: the only difficulty was, that her flamingo was gone across to the other side of the garden, where Alice could see it trying in a helpless sort of way to fly up into a tree.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: By the time she had caught the flamingo and brought it back, the fight was over, and both the hedgehogs were out of sight:

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “but it doesn’t matter much,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: thought Alice,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “as all the arches are gone from this side of the ground.”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: So she tucked it away under her arm, that it might not escape again, and went back for a little more conversation with her friend.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: When she got back to the Cheshire Cat, she was surprised to find quite a large crowd collected round it: there was a dispute going on between the executioner, the King, and the Queen, who were all talking at once, while all the rest were quite silent, and looked very uncomfortable.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The moment Alice appeared, she was appealed to by all three to settle the question, and they repeated their arguments to her, though, as they all spoke at once, she found it very hard indeed to make out exactly what they said.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The executioner’s argument was, that you couldn’t cut off a head unless there was a body to cut it off from: that he had never had to do such a thing before, and he wasn’t going to begin at his time of life.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The King’s argument was, that anything that had a head could be beheaded, and that you weren’t to talk nonsense.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Queen’s argument was, that if something wasn’t done about it in less than no time she’d have everybody executed, all round. (It was this last remark that had made the whole party look so grave and anxious.)

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Alice could think of nothing else to say but

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “It belongs to the Duchess: you’d better ask her about it.”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “She’s in prison,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: the Queen said to the executioner:

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “fetch her here.”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: And the executioner went off like an arrow.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Cat’s head began fading away the moment he was gone, and, by the time he had come back with the Duchess, it had entirely disappeared; so the King and the executioner ran wildly up and down looking for it, while the rest of the party went back to the game.
